obligations.text: Every review job that ends in a review or a visible skip also creates a check run named `statecraft-ai-review` on the reviewed head, in a step after the evidence record is uploaded; its output carries the result as its title and the evidence record byte for byte.

The check run's conclusion is `success` for no-findings, `failure` for findings and `neutral` for any skipped result; it is never a required status context, and ci-gate stays the single context branch protection names.

For a head in this repository, a job that cannot create the check run fails (exit 4), as a review that cannot post its comment does today, so no such result stands without its machine-readable copy. A head in a fork is the one exception: its token cannot create check runs, the step does not run, and review status derives `skipped:fork` from the pull request itself.

The review that counts for a pull request at a head is the newest `statecraft-ai-review` check run on that head whose embedded record names that pull request and that head; a check run naming another pull request or head is ignored, never counted.

`review status <pr>` reads the pull request's current head, or checks `--head <sha>` against it, and reports exactly one outcome: no-findings, findings, skipped:<class>, pending, absent or stale; it never writes, waits, retries, arms or comments.

The exit code follows spec 006 section 3.3: 0 for no-findings; 1 for findings or any skipped result; 2 for pending, absent or stale; 3 for usage; 4 when GitHub cannot be read, classified from the `gh` error stream as spec 012 section 3.5 does.

`absent` names its reason: no statecraft-ci run at the head, a review job that ended cancelled (its duration reported, so a run to the job limit is visible), a review job that failed or refused, or only check runs naming another pull request or head.
The `## AI review` comment, the skip notices, the evidence artifact and how ci-gate reads a review are unchanged.

Step tests run ai-review.sh with a stubbed reviewer and a stubbed gh and find one check run per result, carrying the record; rendering tests show the review job's checks permission and a revision-20 project upgrading in one plan; CLI tests run review status against a stub gh and find every outcome and exit code in section 5, including a newer attempt superseding an older one on one head, a record naming another pull request, and a moved head.

sectionHeadings: 062: The AI review's verdict as a check run, read by `review status`
record.summary: Amends spec 002's setup profile, spec 024's review and spec 006's command surface. github-actions-rust revision 21 publishes every review result (findings, no-findings, skipped:<class>) as a check run on the reviewed head, named `statecraft-ai-review`, whose output carries the evidence record byte for byte. A new read-only verb, `statecraft-cli review status <pr> [--head <sha>] [--repo <owner/name>] [--json]`, reads it under one rule for which review counts, the rule ci-gate already uses in the merge queue, and answers with a closed outcome and spec 006's exit codes. The `## AI review` comment is unchanged. Arming, retrying and waiting are out of scope. Spec 044 moves from revision 21 to revision 22.
record.title: Setup profile revision 21 publishes the AI review's verdict as a check run, and review status reads it
